intent: To highlight the significant disparity between the prevalence of overweight cats and the low awareness of this issue among their owners.

units.meaning: 55% of all household cats are overweight.

basis.entity: 55% of all household cats are overweight
basis.note: The table entity label carries the 55% prevalence; the table value=1.000 is a normalized bar value, not the percentage.

accepted_routes: Overweight prevalence among household cats is 55%
55 percent of all household cats are overweight
units.visual_evidence_rule: A value label or bar/segment for overweight-cat prevalence must read 55%.
units.temporal_anchor: The first narration clause, introducing the 55% prevalence.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state 55% as the overweight prevalence among household cats?

units.meaning: Only 9% of the cats' owners know that.

basis.note: The table entity label carries the 9% owner-awareness value; the table value=1.000 is a normalized bar value, not the percentage.

units.visual_evidence_rule: A value label or bar/segment for owner awareness must read 9%.
units.temporal_anchor: The second narration clause, introduced by the contrast 'but only 9%...'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state 9% as the owner-awareness value?

units.meaning: The disparity between overweight prevalence and owner awareness is 46 percentage points.

basis.entity: 55% of all household cats are overweight
basis.note: First value used in the subtraction.
Second value used in the subtraction.

accepted_routes: There is a 46-point gap between overweight prevalence and owner awareness
Prevalence is 46 points higher than awareness
Only 9% aware versus 55% overweight — a 46-point disparity
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both 55% and 9% must be visible and comparable; the disparity should be shown as a gap/difference, not only as two isolated labels.
units.temporal_anchor: The pivot/contrast between the two narration clauses, or a subsequent comparison beat.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 46-percentage-point gap required to satisfy the intent, or can 55% and 9% alone suffice?

units.meaning: Overweight prevalence is about 6.1 times owner awareness.

basis.entity: 55% of all household cats are overweight

accepted_routes: Overweight prevalence is about 6.1 times owner awareness
Prevalence is over sixfold the awareness rate
units.visual_evidence_rule: If included, a ratio or multiplier annotation, or a side-by-side comparison, must make the roughly 6.1x relation visible.
units.temporal_anchor: Optional comparison beat after both 55% and 9% are established.
units.reviewer_question: Should the optional 6.1x ratio be included, or is the percentage-point gap enough?

units.meaning: 55% represents a majority of household cats.

basis.entity: 55% of all household cats are overweight
basis.note: The 55% prevalence is above half, supporting a majority framing.

accepted_routes: 55% is a majority of household cats
More than half of household cats are overweight
units.visual_evidence_rule: A majority or over-half cue/label should accompany or frame the 55% mark if this framing is used.
units.temporal_anchor: The first narration clause, especially if 55% is introduced as a majority.
units.reviewer_question: Is the majority/more-than-half framing required, or is it only optional color?

optional_valid: Framing the 55% value as a majority or more than half of household cats.
Expressing the disparity as a ratio of about 6.1x instead of only a 46-point gap.
Stating the U.S. context from the original narration, provided it is not presented as table-derived.
Showing both values in the same color because both table rows share color #C0392B.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims such as owners not noticing because cats hide weight gain.
Extrapolating to all pets or to cats outside household cats.
Using 91% of owners do not know unless an explicit 100% denominator is added; it is not directly tabled.
Treating 9% as a share of cats rather than a share of owners.
Treating value=1.000 or relative_value=0.8125 as the 55% or 9% prevalence.
Claiming a change over time or trend; the table has no time variable.
notes: The table stores identical value=1.000 and relative_value=0.8125 for both rows, so the 55% and 9% semantics are taken from the entity labels. The derived 46-point gap and 6.1x ratio are arithmetic from those two label values; do not visualize the normalized cells as the prevalence or awareness.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
